prerequisites.name: Server hardware basics
prerequisites.definition: How a physical server is built: CPU, memory, drives, NICs and firmware, and how servers sit in datacenter racks.
prerequisites.why: A NIC is a server component, so you need a picture of server hardware first.

prerequisites.name: HTTP and web APIs
prerequisites.definition: How clients call servers over HTTP, including headers, status codes and tokens.
prerequisites.why: REST builds on HTTP verbs, URLs and status codes.

prerequisites.name: Linux system administration basics
prerequisites.definition: Configuring users, packages, files and services on a Linux OS.
prerequisites.why: Containers are isolated Linux processes with their own filesystems and packages.

prerequisites.name: Layer 2 Ethernet networking
prerequisites.definition: How switches forward frames by MAC address within a local network segment.
prerequisites.why: IP routing runs on top of Ethernet switching.

prerequisites.name: IP addressing basics
prerequisites.definition: How IP addresses identify hosts on a network.
prerequisites.why: Subnets and routing build on IP addresses.

prerequisites.name: Cryptographic hashing
prerequisites.definition: One-way functions that produce a fixed-size digest of data.
prerequisites.why: Digital signatures sign a hash of the data.

prerequisites.name: Public-key cryptography
prerequisites.definition: Cryptography that uses a public/private key pair for encryption and digital signatures.
prerequisites.why: SSH logs you in with key pairs and checks host keys.

prerequisites.name: IP networking fundamentals
prerequisites.definition: How IP addresses, subnets, switches and routers move packets between machines on Ethernet networks.
prerequisites.why: Firewall rules match on addresses, ports and protocols.

prerequisites.name: Network interface card (NIC)
prerequisites.definition: The hardware that connects a server to a network.
prerequisites.why: MAC addresses belong to NICs, and switches forward frames between NIC ports.
